text:
maria: Heads-up — node gpu-12 had 6 Xid=13s in 20m and the job got retried. I'm proposing a tiny collector agent to grab dmesg/journalctl + nvidia-smi snapshot on first Xid and attach to the node incident card.
jeff: +1 need those artifacts. Current bundles are way too noisy and delayed.
nina: what do you mean by "attach to the node incident card"? where would that live?
maria: short: small gzipped bundle uploaded to our secure blobstore with a per-incident id. Link appears in the SRE incident card. No huge logs, just focused snippets.
omar: rough sketch of what to collect: `dmesg --since "10 minutes ago"` tail last 200 lines, `journalctl -u nvidia-driver --no-pager -n 500`, `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,FB_USAGE --format=csv`, plus a tiny /proc/driver/nvidia/version.
maria: exactly. Also capture kernel oops lines and any `GPU has a single-bit ECC error` messages.
jeff: size cap? we don't want agent to saturate network during noisy node.
maria: cap to 256KB gzip. If bundle > cap, trim oldest lines, and add a `truncated: true` flag in metadata.
nina: metadata schema idea: `incident_id`, `node`, `ts`, `trigger` (Xid/ECC), `collector_version`, `sha256` of bundle, `truncated` boolean. Need that as JSON next to the blob.
omar: sample collector command (proof of concept):
```
#!/bin/bash
OUT=/tmp/gpu-incident-$(date +%s).tar.gz
mkdir /tmp/gpu-incident
dmesg --ctime --since "15 minutes ago" | tail -n 300 > /tmp/gpu-incident/dmesg.txt
journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver -n 800 --no-pager > /tmp/gpu-incident/journal.txt || true
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,FB_USAGE > /tmp/gpu-incident/nvidia-smi.txt || true
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version 2>/dev/null > /tmp/gpu-incident/driver-version.txt || true
python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"node":"$(hostname)","ts":int(__import__("time").time())}))' > /tmp/gpu-incident/meta.json
# gzip cap logic omitted for brevity
tar -czf $OUT -C /tmp gpu-incident
# upload to blobstore API
curl -X POST -F "file=@$OUT" https://blobstore.internal/incidents/upload?node=$(hostname)
```
jeff: love the PoC. We should run it only on Xid types >= 13 or ECC warnings to avoid churn.
maria: agree. Trigger condition: observe Xid 13/31 or ECC report in the kernel ringbuffer, OR `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=error_state --format=csv` shows issues.
omin: (bot) @sre-bot created incident INC-2026-314 for node gpu-12 and linked to 1932104567 thread
sre-bot: Running preflight: will not run collector if node is above 80% network ingress threshold.
jeff: ops question — how do we ensure privacy for customer workloads? some logs might include envs.
omar: we only capture kernel/journal + nvidia-smi; no application logs by design. Mask any environment variables and exclude /var/log/pods. Add a small audit ok.
maria: rollout plan: feature flag behind `gpu_incident_collector` in k8s node agent configmap. Canary to 10 nodes in staging -> 50 in prod -> full. 2-week opt-in for oncall to review bundles.
nina: tests: unit for trimming logic, e2e on a dedicated test rig that injects synthetic Xids and verifies bundle upload and metadata. Add a quick lint for meta.json schema.
jeff: SLO impact? shouldn't affect token bucket. We need rate limit to 1 collector per node per 10m.
maria: implemented as lockfile + rate-limit TTL. Also backoff if upload endpoint returns 429.
omar: question about correlation: include `job_id` and `kube_pod` if present from kube node local cache. Could help triage noisy tenant causing repeated Xids.
maria: we can try to resolve pod-owner via kubelet API when allowed by RBAC, else omit. Field may be null. Documented in schema.
sre-bot: deploy-bot will schedule canary rollout when feature flag is set to true in deploy config.
deploy-bot: started canary deploy 1932104600 -> 10 nodes in staging.
maria: will PR the collector + schema to infra repo today. Assigning reviewers @jeff and @nina.
jeff: I can review this afternoon. Also add a short runbook snippet for oncall: how to fetch bundle, quick grep commands, and when to drain/replace.
maria: thanks — I'll add runbook. If this works, should cut mean time to fingerprint from ~45m to <10m. :rocket: 
omar: one more: add a small fingerprint hash from dmesg top 10 lines to help dedupe repeated incidents across nodes.
maria: noted. OK I'm opening the PR. Will paste it here when ready.
jeff: :thumbsup:
